newsitem.title: FRANCE: Wartime crimes trial of France's Papon finally set.
newsitem.headline: Wartime crimes trial of France's Papon finally set.

text.p: The trial of former cabinet minister Maurice Papon on charges of wartime crimes against humanity will begin on October 8, justice officials said on Thursday.
The officials had told reporters on Wednesday the long-delayed trial would begin on October 6 but they later clarified that jury selection would begin on that date.

There was public outcry last month when justice officials said the trial, delayed by legal moves for more than a decade, might be put back several months because plans to build a large courtroom to accommodate demand for press and public seating were more costly than expected.
The officials said on Wednesday that the proceedings in a courtroom holding 200 people will be projected live on a screen in a nearby hall.
The threat of new delays in the trial of Papon, 86, had angered relatives of his alleged wartime victims who have fought to bring him to justice since 1981.
Papon is accused of ordering the deportation of 1,560 Jews to Nazi death camps in 1942-44 when he served as wartime secretary-general of the Bordeaux region under the Vichy government.
He has denied guilt and insisted he used his position to help the Resistance fighting France's Nazi conquerors.
Papon enjoyed an illustrious post-war career until the discovery of wartime files documenting his arrests and deportation orders.
He served as Paris police chief in 1958-67 and budget minister in the 1970s.
